angle: The undefined spare room is priced by whatever the buyer decides it is, so the photo should decide for them. Three uses, one photograph, camera never moves.
visualSummary: A five slide deep blue swipe deck. Slide one is a tight crop of a completely empty room, white walls, pale oak floor, a window at the left and a door at the right, under a dark scrim with the question what is this room for and a swipe chevron. Slides two, three and four each sit on the deep blue field with a short line, a note and one rounded photo card of the same room staged as an office, then a guest room, then a reading room, each carrying a use pill. The window, radiator, sill, cornice, doorway and floorboards are identical in all three. Slide five is the deep blue closing field with the ask and a single white pill. Warm chalk white and pale oak against the blue chrome.

copy.headline: What is this room for?
copy.caption:
Every house has one room nobody can name. The listing photo has to call it something, and whatever you call it is what the buyer prices.

Empty, that room is a question. We staged the same photograph three times and never moved the camera.

As an office it sells to the buyer who works from home. As a guest room it sells to the buyer whose family visits. As a reading room it sells to the buyer who wants somewhere quiet. Same walls, same window, same floor. Three different buyers.

Go and look at your own gallery. If a room in it has no furniture and no label, the buyer is filling it in for you, and they will fill it in with the version they do not want.

One photo in, seven styles to choose from, free to try.

round1Blocking: Slide 4 armchair: front leg truncated in mid air with no foot and no contact shadow.
Slide 3 wooden armchair: centre rear leg ends in air above the floor.
Slide 2 desk chair: a wooden lounge chair frame fused onto an office gas lift, with a detached spoke fragment floating beside an incoherent star base.
Slide 4 armchair backrest: a detached grey smear floating on the upholstery, meant as steam from a mug but separated from it.
review.howFixed: All four were in the photography, not the layout, so the three renders were redone against the SAME pinned source photograph with prompts naming the failure modes: a plain four leg chair with no gas lift, identical bedside tables, and no mug, steam or vapour anywhere. The scores fell from 85/80/85 to 80/80/80 because the reviewer switched to complaining that an occluded fourth leg is 'missing', which round two of the image review then rejected on inspection. Rule 4 was applied both rounds: every render was opened and looked at.
review.round1Nit: Slide 1's blue accent clause measured about 2.4:1 to 3.5:1 over the scrimmed photo, under the large text floor. Fixed by folding the clause into the white headline rather than lightening the template scrim, which would have restyled shared chrome for one post.
nits: Slide 2 keyboard and mouse are mushy at high zoom. Reads correctly at feed size.
Slide 3 bed's front legs are cut by the bottom edge of the photo card, so no foot lands. A crop artefact, not a truncated leg.
Slide 3 floor reads warmer than slides 2 and 4, mostly genuine shadow cast by the bed.
Slide 5 body copy orphans 'to' at the line break. Rag preference only.
Pseudo lettering on book spines in slides 2 and 4, sub legible at delivered size.
review.dashAudit: Zero hyphens, en dashes or em dashes in any rendered type across all five slides. The only dash-like marks anywhere are photographic: two routed drawer pulls on the slide 2 pedestal.
review.sameRoomVerdict: One room, confirmed by pixel registration rather than impression. The radiator top edge, its fluting count and spacing, the window sill terminus, the doorway architrave, the light switch plate and the door handle all land at the same coordinates across slides 2, 3 and 4, so 'Same window. Same floor.' and 'Camera never moved.' are supported by the pixels.
review.samenessVerdict: Not a rerun. The five legacy thumbnails are all a single frame split before and after by a hard or wavy divider. This is an ordered five slide deck with no split and no before/after badge, arguing 'one photo, three answers' rather than 'empty becomes furnished'.

devilsAdvocate.whyThisOne: It does not ask the viewer to admire a render, it settles an argument they are losing. Every seller with a spare room has been told it should be an office and also that it should be a guest room, and the listing photo has to commit. This shows the photo does not have to commit at all. None of the last ten posts is about what a room is for; all ten are about how a room looks.
devilsAdvocate.whyItEarnsAClick: The only way to find out which version their own room wants is to put their own photo in. Carousels also out-view Reels below 5K followers, take about nine times the saves of a single image, and get re-served on swipe-through.
devilsAdvocate.howItDiffers: The last three published frames are all fullbleed photos split by a seam. This is an ordered swipe deck with a fixed camera and a hook slide, on a cooler and lighter field than the recent warm-wood run.
devilsAdvocate.residualRisk: The deck lives or dies on the three frames sharing walls, window, floor and camera. If the model drifts the background between slides, the post silently argues the opposite of its own headline.
devilsAdvocate.authorNote: The advocate picked i22 as a Masking Studio post. There is no mask path anywhere in this tooling: lib/images/acquire.js only calls processStaging on a whole photo, so 'only the furniture region changed' could not be honestly claimed. featureShown was moved to ai-designer, which is what actually produced the three variants (three typed instructions against one source photo), and no copy claims pixel identity. The renders held the architecture on their own, which is why the post still works.
